title: 183 GHz Water Megamasers in Active Galactic Nuclei: A New Accretion Disk Tracer
question: Identify and characterize 183 GHz H2O megamaser emission from AGN already known to host 22 GHz megamaser systems, and compare their spectral and spatial properties to 22 GHz masers.

data.angular_resolution: ~0.6 arcseconds at 183 GHz (for Circinus); arcsecond-scale nominal beam
data.sensitivity: typical spectral sensitivity of ~2 mJy per ~2 km s^-1 (1.2 to 21.8 mJy); continuum RMS 0.05 to 1.13 mJy arcsec^-2

what.value: 22 GHz spectra, peak flux densities, and isotropic luminosities for NGC 1194, ESO 558-G009, IC 485, J0847-0022, Mrk 1419, IC 2560, UGC 6093, CGCG 074-064, NGC 5495, and NGC 5765b

evidence.quote: Our 183 GHz spectrum of NGC 1194 is shown in the upper lefthand panel of [1](#fig:hex1), along with a 22 GHz spectrum reproduced from (cite: Pesce_2015) (see Fig. 1 in that paper).
This value is a factor of $\sim$2 lower than the $\sim$130 L$_{\odot}$ isotropic luminosity observed at 22 GHz (cite: Pesce_2015).

what.value: 22 GHz spectra and isotropic luminosities for ESO 269-G012 and NGC 5643

evidence.quote: Our 183 GHz spectrum of ESO 269-G012 is shown in the upper righthand panel of [2](#fig:hex2), along with a 22 GHz spectrum reproduced from (cite: Greenhill_2003b) (see Fig. 1 in that paper).
This value is a factor of $\sim$2 higher than the $\sim$12.6 L$_{\odot}$ isotropic luminosity observed at 22 GHz (cite: Greenhill_2003b).

what.value: 22 GHz spectrum and isotropic luminosity for Circinus

evidence.quote: Our 183 GHz spectrum of Circinus is shown in the lefthand panel of [3](#fig:Circinus), along with a 22 GHz spectrum reproduced from (cite: Braatz_2003).
This value is a factor of $\sim$2.5 higher than the $\sim$73 L$_{\odot}$ isotropic luminosity observed at 22 GHz (cite: Braatz_2003).

what.value: VLBI 22 GHz map and edge-on disk midline of Circinus

evidence.quote: To compare more directly with the 22 GHz maser distribution, we overplot in [3](#fig:Circinus) the midline of the edge-on disk inferred in (cite: Greenhill_2003).

what.value: Symmetrized distance measurement of 87.6 +/- 7.5 Mpc to CGCG 074-064

evidence.quote: Adopting the symmetrized $87.6 \pm 7.5$ Mpc distance measurement from (cite: Pesce_2020), the isotropic luminosity of the 183 GHz maser emission from CGCG 074-064 is $L_{\text{iso}} \approx 484$ L$_{\odot}$.

what.value: Type Ia Supernova distance of 12.4 +/- 0.5 Mpc to NGC 5643

evidence.quote: Because NGC 5643 is nearby enough that the Hubble law distance is expected to be very uncertain, we instead adopt a Type Ia Supernova distance of $12.4 \pm 0.5$ Mpc to this system from (cite: Burns_2020).
Adopting the $126.3 \pm 11.6$ Mpc distance from (cite: Gao_2016), the isotropic luminosity of the 183 GHz maser emission from NGC 5765b is $L_{\text{iso}} \approx 379$ L$_{\odot}$.

what.value: Tully-Fisher distance measurement of 4.2 +/- 0.8 Mpc to Circinus

evidence.quote: Because Circinus is nearby enough that the Hubble law distance is very uncertain, we instead adopt the Tully-Fisher distance measurement of $4.2 \pm 0.8$ Mpc to this system from (cite: Karachentsev_2013).

recipe.goal: Calibrate raw ALMA visibility data and concatenate multi-epoch observations
recipe.method: Import raw ASDM files to MSs, flag pointing scans/autocorrelations/shadowed antennas and manual edge/initial channels, apply Tsys and WVR tables, solve bandpass and phase/amplitude gains, bootstrap absolute flux scale using power-law interpolation of ALMA calibrator catalog, self-calibrate Circinus on the brightest line, and concatenate multi-day MSs.
key_parameters: Bandpass pre-gaincal averaging over ~5% of each spectral window per integration time
Circinus phase self-calibration: 3 channels (~0.6 km s^-1) centered at 561.6 km s^-1, solint = 60 seconds
assumptions: Power-law spectral energy distribution S_nu = S_{nu,0} (nu / nu_0)^alpha for flux density calibrators

recipe.goal: Image spectral line cubes and continuum maps
recipe.method: Deconvolve Stokes I visibilities using Högbom CLEAN in CASA tclean for each channel to produce image cubes, and combine line-free channels/windows for continuum images.
key_parameters: natural weighting, standard gridding, 300x300 pixels, pixel size ~1/8 nominal beam FWHM, loop gain = 0.1, stopping criterion peak residual ~5x expected RMS, no CLEAN boxes

recipe.goal: Identify 183 GHz spectral line detections and measure peak flux densities and sensitivities
recipe.method: Extract spectra from the central region of each image cube, apply 10-channel boxcar smoothing in frequency, compute RMS across the full spectral window, and identify peaks reaching >= 5 sigma across multiple channels.
key_parameters: boxcar smoothing = 10 channels (~2 km s^-1 resolution); detection threshold >= 5 sigma across multiple channels; continuum nondetection threshold < 3 sigma

recipe.goal: Compute 183 GHz isotropic maser luminosities and compare with 22 GHz spectra
recipe.method: Integrate the 183 GHz flux density over velocity and compute isotropic luminosity L_iso using adopted source distances, and compare qualitatively and quantitatively with literature 22 GHz spectra.
key_parameters: Rest frequency nu_0 = 183.310087 GHz; H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; peculiar velocity uncertainty = 300 km s^-1
assumptions: Isotropic emission for L_iso; H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 and 300 km s^-1 peculiar velocity uncertainty for Hubble law distances

recipe.goal: Map 183 GHz maser spot positions in Circinus via visibility modeling
recipe.method: Fit a point source model directly to the self-calibrated, time-averaged Stokes I complex visibilities in each spectral channel individually using nested sampling.
key_parameters: Plot threshold: geometric mean positional uncertainty sqrt(sigma_x * sigma_y) < 20 mas; reference maser spot at v = 561.6 km s^-1
assumptions: Each maser spot in a spectral channel is a single point source; noise sigma is constant across visibilities within a single channel; brightest 183 GHz spot at 561.6 km s^-1 corresponds to the 22 GHz reference spot at 566.3 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Fit and map serendipitous molecular lines (HNC and HC3N) in Circinus and NGC 1068
recipe.method: Image continuum spectral window cubes with CASA tclean and fit a 1D Gaussian plus constant continuum background to the spectrum at every pixel location using scipy curve_fit.
key_parameters: 4 free parameters per pixel: constant background S_0, peak brightness A, center velocity v_0, standard deviation sigma
assumptions: Single Gaussian line profile per pixel; pixel uncertainty equal to continuum RMS level

answer_key.quantity: Number of 183 GHz maser detections out of 20 AGN surveyed

evidence.quote: Out of 20 sources observed, we detect significant 183 GHz maser emission from 13; this survey thus increases the number of AGN known to host (sub)millimeter megamasers by a factor of 5.

answer_key.quantity: NGC 1194 peak 183 GHz flux density (unsmoothed narrow high-velocity line at 4593.5 km s^-1)
NGC 1194 peak 183 GHz flux density (smoothed systemic features)

evidence.quote: The peak flux density after smoothing over 10 channels occurs in the systemic set of features and reaches a value of $\sim$16 mJy.

answer_key.quantity: Circinus peak 183 GHz flux density (native ~0.2 km s^-1 resolution)

score_reason: Exceptionally thorough calibration, imaging, and visibility-modeling description (including CASA version, exact calibrator flux densities and spectral indices in Table 3, tclean parameters, and exact likelihood/priors for dynesty). Minor deductions only for unstated spectral extraction aperture and velocity integration windows, plus inclusion of some non-QA2 blocks.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data with two clearly stated project codes, complete calibration/imaging/modeling parameters, and well-defined quantitative answer keys (peak flux densities, RMS sensitivities, isotropic luminosities in Table 2, and Circinus astrometric map).
